tasks.q: Why is data compressed? Select all that apply.
opts: To make the data impossible to read
To add more colours to an image
tasks.fb: Making data unreadable is encryption, which is a different thing.

tasks.q: Which is a benefit of compression for a video streaming service?
a: Video can be sent over slower connections without buffering
It removes the need for servers
tasks.fb: Less data per second means fewer interruptions.

tasks.q: What happens to the data in lossy compression?
a: Some is permanently removed, so the original can't be restored
It is rearranged but all kept
tasks.fb: That's why it's called lossy: data is lost.

tasks.q: Which file types typically use lossy compression?
tasks.fb: Photos and music can lose detail without most people noticing.

tasks.q: What is the key feature of lossless compression?
a: The original file can be restored exactly
It always gives the smallest file

tasks.q: Why must text and program files use lossless compression?
a: Losing even one character or instruction would corrupt the file
They are too small to compress
Lossy compression is illegal for text
tasks.fb: A program with missing bits simply won't run.

tasks.q: Which type of compression should be used for each file?
items: A photo on a web page
A video on a streaming service
tasks.fb: If losing detail would break the file, it has to be lossless.

tasks.q: Copy this image, then look at each row: how many runs does it have?
tasks.fb: Rows of repeated pixels compress well with run-length encoding.
tasks.title: Colour the grid

tasks.q: A row of 8 pixels is 00001111. How would run-length encoding store it?
a: Colour 0 four times, then colour 1 four times
The average colour of the row
tasks.fb: Two runs instead of eight values.

tasks.q: When does run-length encoding work best?
a: When the image has large areas of the same colour
When every pixel is a different colour
When the image is a photograph
When the image is in colour

tasks.q: What happens if RLE is used on an image where every pixel differs from the next?
a: The compressed file can be larger than the original
tasks.fb: Each run of one still needs a count stored.

tasks.q: Is each statement about lossy or lossless compression?
items: The original file can be restored exactly
Used for MP3 and JPEG files
Used for text and program files
tasks.fb: Lossy trades quality for size; lossless keeps everything.

tasks.q: A 1-bit image row is 11111000. How many runs does run-length encoding need?
Why is compression especially important for streaming video?
a: It reduces the bandwidth needed, so video plays without buffering
tasks.fb: Less data per second is the whole point.

info.title: ZIP
info.text: ZIP files use lossless compression, which is why a zipped document opens exactly as it was, character for character.

info.title: JPEG artefacts
info.text: Save a JPEG repeatedly and it slowly degrades: each save throws a little more detail away.

info.title: Fax machines
info.text: Run-length encoding is old technology: fax machines used it to send pages of mostly white paper quickly.

info.title: Streaming
info.text: Video services compress the same film at several quality levels and switch between them as your connection changes.

info.title: Lossless audio
info.text: Formats like FLAC compress music losslessly, giving files around half the size of raw audio with no quality loss.

info.title: Already compressed
info.text: Zipping a JPEG saves almost nothing: the file has already had its patterns squeezed out.
